subject: Hosted API: token chokepoint causing p99 regression & 429 amplification
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@alphaprod.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Immediate: Hosted API p99 spike and recurring 429s causing timeouts

Hi Naomi —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 response times and a flurry of 429s around 08:30 PT. This is impacting two of our customer-facing flows (payment validation and chat summarization); threads are timing out and our frontend is retrying aggressively which looks to be amplifying the tail.

Key observations from our side:
- p95 ~ 1.1s -> 2.8s; p99 ~ 2.6s -> 8.9s within 30 minutes
- 429s spike aligns with a configuration change we received yesterday (rate limit weight per token applied)
- Retries are queued and we observe increased client-side timeouts after ~6s

We need an urgent mitigation: can you temporarily remove/reduce the new per-token weight for our account or open a higher rate cap? Also sharing request_for_evidence.pdf with sample traces.

Please advise ETA; this is causing revenue-impacting user errors.

— Jane Saito
SRE, AlphaProd

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@alphaprod.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Hosted API p99 spike and recurring 429s causing timeouts

Jane —

Thanks for the heads-up and the traces. I’m escalating immediately. Looping in our ops and eng leads. We’ll confirm mitigation within 30 minutes.

Short plan: 1) I’ll request a temporary cap increase for AlphaProd, 2) ask infra to roll back the per-token weight change for your tenant, 3) engineering to enable conservative global backoff on the proxy to break retry amplification.

I’ll follow up once we have the rollback/adjustment scheduled.

— Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0191

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@alphaprod.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Immediate: Hosted API p99 spike and recurring 429s causing timeouts

Team — forwarding an urgent customer escalation from AlphaProd. They’ve attached traces and called out that yesterday’s change to per-token rate weighting lines up with the spike. They are seeing substantial p99 regressions and retry amplification from their frontend.

Ask: Can infra/serving roll back the per-token weight change for AlphaProd immediately (or open a temporary higher cap) and enable proxy-level global backoff so we stop the amplification? AlphaProd is on a dedicated burst plan; we should be able to make this change from the control plane.

Customer impact: revenue flows and chat summarization user journeys. Execs are likely to be involved if we can’t provide a fast fix.

Attachments: request_for_evidence.pdf (sample traces)

Naomi

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Immediate: Hosted API p99 spike and recurring 429s causing timeouts

Naomi / Sean / Laura —

Thanks for the flag, Naomi. Quick technical summary from logs and early diagnostics (I pulled the logset link and the attached p99_graph):
- Root cause hypothesis: the new per-token weight change introduced a hard "token-chokepoint" in the capacity allocator for multi-tenant queues. For accounts with bursty long-context requests (AlphaProd), the effective QPS drops unevenly and workers backpressure, increasing queueing latency and producing 429s at proxy-level.
- Retry amplification: client retries (default 3 attempts) surface as bursts that slot into already backpressured queues, amplifying p99.

Immediate remediation plan (proposed, can be executed in parallel):
1) Roll back the per-token weight change for tenant AlphaProd (control plane change, immediate) — target T+8m
2) Temporarily raise tenant rate cap by 2x for 45 minutes to drain queues — T+10m
3) Enable conservative global backoff at the proxy (10% jittered exponential, max backoff 2s) to prevent synchronized retries — T+12m
4) Run temporary canary traffic with reduced fanout to validate p99 improvement before fully restoring policy — T+20m
5) Produce a short incident note with traces and timeline and deliver to AlphaProd and our execs — T+60m

I’ve attached the p99_graph-20270118.png that shows queueing tail growth. I’ll coordinate with infra SRE to execute steps 1–3 now. Laura — can you authorize the temporary cap increase from Commercial? Sean — I’ll need an exec on standby for customer communications if this slips.

-Markus
VP, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Jane Saito <jane.saito@alphaprod.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API incident & next steps

Jane —

Appreciate the clear traces. We’re treating this as high priority. Naomi, Markus and I are moving the mitigation now per Markus’s plan.

Immediate customer-facing items:
- We’ll keep you updated every 20 minutes for the next 2 hours.
- If mitigation does not fully resolve customer impact, we will apply a credit for the affected window. I’ll prepare the remediation/credit proposal in parallel.

Naomi — I’ll prep a short exec note and stand by for any ask on commercial concessions.

— Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales, Customer Success (Americas)
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@alphaprod.com>, Jane Saito <jane.saito@alphaprod.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Incident update: rollbacks applied, backoff enabled, next steps

Hi Jane / AlphaProd team —

Quick update following yesterday’s incident and our remediation work:

What we did (completed):
- Rolled back the per-token weight change for AlphaProd at 09:38 PT (control plane entry reverted)
- Raised tenant rate cap 2x for 45 minutes to allow queues to drain (09:40–10:25 PT)
- Enabled conservative proxy-level global backoff and jitter to reduce synchronized retries (09:42 PT)

Observations:
- p95 and p99 fell back to expected range within ~18 minutes of rollback; p99 returned to baseline by 10:00 PT. See attached p99_graph-20270118.png.
- We observed continued client retry spikes for ~30 minutes after the rollback — we recommend adjusting client-side retry logic to include jitter and exponential backoff (we can share suggested config).

Next steps:
1) Post-incident report with timeline, traces and recommended configuration changes (will deliver by EOD today). Link to working notes: https://drive.redwood.com/notes/DEAL-8342/diagnostic-logset
2) Engagement to review AlphaProd's client retry settings and recommend safer defaults (optional workshop)
3) Follow-up run at 72h to validate no regression after we reintroduce optimized token-weighting with safer queue isolation controls

We understand the impact this had on your users; Sean will follow up on remediation/credit terms. We’ll keep you notified on the post-incident note.

Thanks for your patience and for providing the traces — they were crucial to diagnosing the token-chokepoint behavior quickly.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
